title: Risk Assessment: Make `make test` changeset-aware
summary: Technical risk assessment for introducing a static reverse import-graph (grimp) driven test selector with a per-branch sidecar LKG, defaulting `make test` to narrowed selection and routing CI to `make test-all`. Overall risk is MEDIUM. The refine-phase decisions (sidecar over tracked file, grimp over hand-rolled, scan-during-graph-construction for dynamic imports, canary-every-10th, stderr+JSON logging, full-suite-on-non-py) close most of the obvious holes; what remains is a concentrated correctness risk around silent false negatives from edges the static graph cannot see (gateway's importlib-based test loader, cross-root edges, pytest plugin discovery) and a modest set of integration risks around CI/sandbox environments, Makefile edge cases, and PYTEST_ARGS semantics. The full-suite escape hatch (`make test-all`) plus canary mode makes the worst-case blast radius recoverable, but correctness-first acceptance criteria are only honored if the dynamic-import and cross-package fallback rules are implemented carefully.

decision-7 (`make test` narrowed default; `make test-all` full)
decision-8 (sidecar untracked, moot for gateway push policy)
decision-10 (scan during graph construction for dynamic-import modules; widen reachable)
decision-11 (N/A under decision-2 since CI uses test-all)

risks.title: Silent false negatives: static graph misses gateway's importlib-based test loading
risks.impact: Changes to gateway/ production modules may not select gateway/tests/* because gateway/tests/conftest.py loads production modules with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location — grimp sees no static import edge from gateway/tests/test_*.py back to gateway/<module>.py. A green narrow run then advances LKG with a latent regression, which is *exactly* the failure mode the correctness-first acceptance criterion forbids.
risks.description: gateway/tests/conftest.py contains a `_load_module_with_replaced_imports` helper (module-level code around lines 47-85) that string-replaces relative imports and loads modules by file path, then stuffs them into sys.modules under both the bare name and the `gateway.` prefix. grimp's static AST scan sees neither the replaced-import text nor the dynamic load target. Result: if a coder changes gateway/gateway.py, grimp computes the reverse closure against what it can see (no edge from gateway/tests/test_*.py → gateway/gateway.py in the static graph) and selects zero gateway tests. Decision-10 partially compensates: conftest.py contains `importlib.util` calls, so it lands in the dynamic-import-marker set. But the widening rule is 'widen only if a changed module is in (or reachable from) that set' — production gateway modules are NOT reachable FROM conftest.py under static analysis, because static analysis doesn't see conftest.py → production_module edges either.

mitigation.strategy: Add gateway/tests/ to an explicit 'always-widen' list keyed on a changed path matching `gateway/*.py`. Equivalently, treat the gateway/tests/conftest.py dynamic-import annotation as a DOWNSTREAM marker: if the conftest uses importlib to load siblings of a changed production module, any change under that production directory pulls the co-located test directory into the selected set. The task plan must specify this explicitly; it cannot be silently inferred from decision-10's generic 'reachable from' widening because the static graph has no edge to traverse. Recommend: hard-code a mapping {gateway/*.py: include gateway/tests/} into the selector's fallback-trigger table, documented as a known static-analysis blind spot.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — the mapping is small and stable; if other dirs grow importlib-based test loaders, they must be added to the map

risks.review_reason: Correctness-first is the primary acceptance criterion. This failure mode silently smuggles regressions into LKG and cascades. Reviewer must confirm the special case for gateway/tests/ is explicit in the plan, not an implicit consequence of decision-10.

risks.title: Cross-root import edges dropped if grimp is not invoked with all repo roots
risks.impact: grimp.build_graph resolves imports only within the packages it was told about. If called with a single root, cross-root edges (e.g., gateway importing from shared.egg_contracts, or orchestrator importing from shared.egg_config) are silently treated as external and excluded. Changes to shared/ would then fail to pull in gateway/tests/ or orchestrator/tests/ — directly violating AC-2 ('Changes to `shared/` modules correctly pull in tests across gateway/, orchestrator/, and sandbox/ that import them').
risks.description: The repo has at least 5 top-level root packages on PYTHONPATH or as source dirs: gateway, shared, orchestrator, sandbox, tests (plus sandbox/tools, integration_tests). The Makefile's `test` target sets PYTHONPATH to `shared:gateway:orchestrator`. grimp must be invoked with every root whose imports need to be traced. If the selector invokes `grimp.build_graph('gateway', 'shared', 'orchestrator')` but omits `sandbox` or `tests`, the sandbox→shared and tests→shared edges are missing. Since `tests/` contains test files that import from shared, sandbox, and config directories, omitting it would make shared/ changes select zero root-level tests.
affected_files: The new test-selection module (wherever it lives)

mitigation.strategy: Enumerate roots explicitly in the selector module with a constant. Include every directory that contains .py files that may be exercised by a test: gateway, shared, orchestrator, sandbox, sandbox/tools, tests, tests/egg_config, tests/functional, tests/security, tests/sandbox, tests/scripts, tests/action, tests/workflows (if present), sandbox/tests, scripts/tests. Add an assertion in the selector: enumerate all .py files under those roots and verify they appear as nodes in graph.modules; log any missing file and fall back to full suite. Add a unit test that constructs a synthetic cross-root import and verifies the reverse closure resolves it.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW if all roots are enumerated; cross-root failures would be caught by the enumeration assertion's full-suite fallback

risks.review_reason: Meeting AC-2 depends on this being right. The task plan must explicitly list the roots.

risks.title: Sandbox test loader and agent code paths are not in the default `make test` target today — verify selector scope matches or over-selects
risks.impact: The current Makefile `test` target only runs `tests/ gateway/tests/ orchestrator/tests/ shared/tests/`. It does NOT run `sandbox/tests/` or `scripts/tests/`. The new selector must preserve this scope (don't *add* tests that weren't being run) OR explicitly broaden it — whichever is intended. Ambiguity here could either (a) silently add new tests to the default path, breaking reproducibility, or (b) miss a changed sandbox/ module because the selector's root list excludes sandbox/tests/.
risks.description: `make test PYTEST_ARGS='...'` today runs only four test-dir arguments. The narrowed selector will pass a discovered subset to pytest. If the selector computes reverse closures across sandbox/, it will produce sandbox/tests/ candidates — passing those to pytest will run sandbox tests that `make test` never ran before (accidental scope expansion). Conversely, if the selector's roots exclude sandbox/, a change in sandbox/ may select zero tests even though a sibling test would have caught the regression.

mitigation.strategy: Define the selector's OUTPUT scope explicitly: the selected set must be a SUBSET of the pre-existing `make test` test universe (tests/ + gateway/tests/ + orchestrator/tests/ + shared/tests/, minus functional-marker). Build the graph across ALL roots (so edges are correct) but filter the final selected-tests set to only include files under those four directories. If a change in sandbox/ cannot be traced to any test in the narrowed universe, fall back to full suite (conservative) — log which change triggered the fallback.

risks.title: Canary rate (every 10th) leaves a ≤9-run window for silent regressions to smuggle into LKG
risks.impact: Q4 selected 'canary every 10th run'. Between canaries, a green narrow run advances LKG whenever a `make test-all` happens to fire (per decision-1 sidecar is auto-updated on any green test-all, independent of canary). Canary kicks in only for `make test`. A silent miss in narrow selection produces no alarm — the selector thought it was right, the run was green, the branch moves on. If the LKG is advanced via a test-all that also has a blind spot, the regression cascades until CI (which runs test-all full) catches it at PR time. Given CI uses test-all (decision-2), the worst-case blast radius is 'PR is red at CI-time' rather than 'regression reaches main'.
risks.description: Full-suite runs happen at CI time, at canary time, and whenever the user/agent runs `make test-all` manually. If an agent iterates with `make test` for ~9 cycles and never hits canary, a bad selection could keep a regression invisible locally. The PR will still go red at CI, which is the safety net. But the agent feedback loop is polluted for up to 9 cycles.
affected_files: selector canary counter (sidecar-adjacent file, per branch)

mitigation.strategy: Make the canary cadence configurable (default 10, CI can pass a different value). Log a prominent 'canary run — full suite selected' line so agents notice the cadence. Additionally, consider a 'last-canary-at' timestamp so branches that sit idle still canary on first reinvocation. Counter persistence: store next to the sidecar — `.egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.canary` — last-writer-wins is acceptable (at worst, a branch gets canaries slightly more or less often than 1-in-10).
mitigation.residual_risk: MEDIUM — the 1-in-10 window is intentional per Q4, not an implementation bug, but it's the residual correctness risk the plan accepts

risks.title: PYTEST_ARGS parsing ambiguity (Q5 intersect-vs-bypass)
risks.impact: Q5 said: 'intersect by default; bypass narrowing only when the user passes explicit test file paths (e.g., PYTEST_ARGS="gateway/tests/test_specific.py")'. Detecting 'explicit file paths' from an arbitrary PYTEST_ARGS string is a parse-this-shell-blob problem: arg could be a file path, a -k expression, a --cov flag, a -m marker, a pytest plugin option, or a mix. Getting this wrong means either (a) agent runs `make test PYTEST_ARGS='gateway/tests/test_specific.py'` and the selector narrows FURTHER than intended, or (b) CI runs `make test-all PYTEST_ARGS='--cov=...'` (decision-2) and the selector mistakenly treats --cov as a path.
risks.description: Shell-style argument parsing in Make is brittle. A naive substring check for '/' in $(PYTEST_ARGS) will false-positive on paths embedded in --cov-report=file.xml; a full shlex parse means reimplementing pytest's own argument logic. The simple answer — 'if any bare positional arg exists in PYTEST_ARGS, bypass narrowing' — is fragile against plugin options like `--hypothesis-seed=42`.

mitigation.strategy: Sidestep shell-parsing entirely by introducing an opt-out env var: `EGG_TEST_SELECT=off make test PYTEST_ARGS='gateway/tests/test_specific.py'`. Default is 'on' (narrow). Document the env var in docs/guides/testing.md. This removes the inference step and makes the behavior user-explicit. If you still want automatic detection, use Python's shlex.split on $(PYTEST_ARGS) and classify each token: tokens that (a) don't start with '-' AND (b) point to an existing file path OR a path-like expression matching `**/test_*.py` OR `**/tests/**.py` count as 'explicit path' tokens — if any are present, bypass narrowing. Add unit tests for tricky PYTEST_ARGS examples (--cov=path, -k pattern, --hypothesis-seed=N, explicit file, mixed).
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW if env var approach is chosen; MEDIUM if shlex heuristics

risks.review_reason: Reviewer should confirm the env-var-opt-out vs shlex-heuristic decision. Q5's recommendation implies heuristic, but explicit env var is more robust.

risks.title: grimp graph-build cost could dominate fast-path latency
risks.impact: grimp reads every .py file in all roots and builds the import graph. For ~771 files on a cold cache, build time could be 1-5s; with grimp's disk cache it drops to <500ms. If the selector is invoked on every `make test`, graph-build may exceed the pytest savings for small diffs.
risks.description: grimp 3.x ships with a Rust backend and disk cache (default cache_dir ~/.grimp_cache or similar). First invocation on a fresh checkout is slow; subsequent invocations are cheap. In a sandbox container that is torn down and recreated per agent invocation, the cache is cold every time unless the cache path is mounted on a persistent volume.

mitigation.strategy: Point grimp's cache_dir to `.egg-state/grimp-cache/` (per-workspace, checked into .gitignore). Mount that path into sandboxes so successive agent invocations reuse the cache. Instrument the selector to log graph-build wall time; if it exceeds a threshold (say 3s), surface a warning. Provide an escape hatch: EGG_TEST_SELECT=off falls back to full suite and skips grimp entirely (covered in R5 mitigation).
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — grimp's cache reduces cost to milliseconds; Rust backend is fast

risks.title: .egg-state/selection/<sha>.json grows unbounded over time
risks.impact: Q15 chose to log a JSON record per run in .egg-state/selection/<sha>.json. Every run writes one file; a branch that runs `make test` 500 times leaves 500 JSON files. Gitignored but accumulates on disk; over months a developer machine or long-lived sandbox volume could grow hundreds of MBs.
risks.description: One JSON record per run is small (kilobytes), but unbounded over time. Equivalent concern for `.egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha` — long-dead branches linger. No natural GC.

mitigation.strategy: Add a simple age-based cleanup: on each `make test` invocation, prune .egg-state/selection/*.json files older than N days (default 14). For .egg-state/last-known-good/*.sha, prune entries whose branch no longer exists in `git branch -a` output. Implement both as a best-effort step — failures to prune don't fail the run. Document cleanup behavior in docs/guides/testing.md.

risks.title: `make test` outside a git checkout or with an unfetched baseline falls back silently
risks.impact: If `make test` runs inside an extracted tarball, a shallow clone where origin/main isn't reachable, or CI environments with fetch-depth=1 (all not-test-all paths), the baseline resolution fails. Decision-11 called this N/A because CI uses test-all — but sandbox agents may run `make test` in shallow checkouts too.
risks.description: Baseline resolution order: (1) sidecar LKG if valid ancestor of HEAD, else (2) $(BASE_BRANCH)=origin/main. If origin/main isn't fetched locally (shallow clone), the `git diff` fails or produces wrong output. The fallback is 'no baseline → full suite', but if the git command is allowed to silently produce an empty diff (e.g., `git rev-parse origin/main` returns a bogus sha), the selector could select zero tests. That's a correctness issue dressed as a configuration issue.

mitigation.strategy: In the selector, explicitly validate: `git merge-base --is-ancestor $BASELINE HEAD` must return 0 for both LKG and base-branch candidates. Any failure → full suite with explicit log reason ('baseline unreachable'). Add a unit test with a shallow-clone fixture.

risks.title: Parallel sandboxes on the same branch race the sidecar (accepted behavior per Q9)
risks.impact: Multiple agent containers can be attached to the same branch (BRC agents in plan phase, implement phase). If two simultaneously run `make test-all` and write .egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha, the last writer wins. Both shas represent green states, so correctness is preserved, but file churn and the potential for torn writes (partial file) exist on non-atomic filesystems.
risks.description: POSIX rename is atomic on the same filesystem. A naive `echo $sha > file.sha` is NOT atomic — a reader mid-write could see truncated content. Ensure writes are via `write-temp-then-rename`.

mitigation.strategy: Write sidecar with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile + os.replace to guarantee atomicity. Validate on read: sidecar must be exactly 40 hex chars (per decision-4) plus optional newline; malformed → treat as absent (use base branch).

risks.title: Backward compat: external callers of `make test` see behavior change
risks.impact: `make test` default behavior flips from 'full suite' to 'changeset-aware'. Callers that assumed `make test` runs everything — pre-commit hooks, developer muscle memory, release scripts, ad-hoc local test runs, Docker build steps, integration scripts — now get a partial run unless they opt in to `make test-all`. Silent behavioral changes are the worst kind for trust.
risks.description: Scan for callers: .github/workflows/*.yml (decision-2 already switches unit-tests job to test-all), integration_tests/ setup, scripts/, CONTRIBUTING.md, README references, docs/ references, sandbox Dockerfiles (if any invoke make test during image build). Any call site that assumed full-suite behavior must be audited.

mitigation.strategy: Grep the repo for literal `make test` in all files (excluding .venv, .git, node_modules). Audit each match; swap to `make test-all` where full-suite behavior is required. Prominent announcement in the PR description, CONTRIBUTING.md diff, and docs/guides/testing.md. Consider printing a one-line banner on `make test` for the first N days post-merge: 'make test is now changeset-aware — use make test-all for the full suite. See docs/guides/testing.md.'
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW after audit; banner provides transition grace period

risks.review_reason: Reviewer should confirm all `make test` call sites have been enumerated and audited. A missed caller could get surprising behavior in production release/automation paths.

risks.title: Non-Python resource fallback (decision-5) is coarse — docs-only PRs trigger full suite
risks.impact: Decision-5 says any non-.py change triggers full suite. A PR that edits only docs/*.md or CHANGELOG.md runs the entire test suite for no correctness reason. This is the conservative v1 choice and is acceptable, but it caps the realistic speedup ceiling for docs-heavy branches.
risks.description: Acceptable for v1 per decision-5. Future optimization (follow-up issue) could introduce an allowlist of 'safe' non-.py paths — .md, LICENSE, images. Documented as Q10/Q8 follow-up appetite.

mitigation.strategy: Log the trigger cause per Q7 ('falling back: docs/index.md changed, non-.py policy'). Open a follow-up issue for v2 allowlist optimization. No code change required in v1.

risks.title: pytest plugin discovery and conftest import side effects not captured by grimp
risks.impact: pytest auto-discovers conftest.py files at collection time via its own mechanism. If a selected test file inherits fixtures from a parent conftest (e.g., tests/sandbox/test_*.py using tests/conftest.py), pytest handles that naturally when running. But grimp's static graph doesn't model conftest-fixture reach. More subtle: pytest_plugins, entry-point plugins, and conftest rootdir discovery. These patterns are covered by decision-10's dynamic-import scan IF the plugin registration uses importlib/__import__, but NOT if it uses `from X import Y` at module top.
risks.description: Shared fixture modules under shared/tests/ (referenced in Q2's 'shared-fixture fallback enumeration') are the highest-risk class. If a shared fixture module is changed and a test depends on it only via conftest fixture injection (not a static import), grimp's reverse closure will miss the dependency.

mitigation.strategy: Add any conftest.py change (root or package-level) to the fallback-trigger list (already listed in Q3 as accepted). In addition, treat any shared/tests/ change as a full-suite trigger for v1 (as recommended in Q2 starting rule). Defer fine-grained shared-fixture mapping to a follow-up issue once real selection-miss data is available (Q8 follow-up appetite).

risks.title: grimp dev dependency adds a Rust-compiled supply-chain surface
risks.impact: grimp 3.x ships as a Rust-compiled wheel. Adding it to dev dependencies introduces a new supply-chain link. No known CVEs (Snyk 2025-10-02), active maintenance (seddonym, v3.14 2025-12-10, 116k weekly downloads), healthy reputation.
risks.description: Dev-only dependency; not shipped in production containers (gateway/orchestrator Dockerfiles COPY dev deps only if needed for tests, which they don't). Risk surface limited to CI and developer machines. uv.lock pins the version; PyPI's 2025 ZIP-confusion mitigations apply.

mitigation.strategy: Pin grimp to a specific minor version range (e.g., grimp>=3.14,<4). Include in Dependabot's weekly scan. Verify grimp is NOT copied into production container images (gateway/Dockerfile, orchestrator/Dockerfile). Add bandit/safety checks in the security scan if they aren't already scanning dev deps (they do).

risks.title: Read-only agent phases that run `make test` would read the sidecar (Q13 says they shouldn't)
risks.impact: Q13 decided read-only phases (refiner, reviewer_*) always use base-branch baseline. But the implementation must actively detect 'read-only phase' — the sidecar file is on disk and accessible to every container. If the selector is a simple Python module invoked by `make test`, it has no phase awareness unless an env var signals it.
risks.description: The sandbox entrypoint sets role-relevant env vars (EGG_AGENT_ROLE, .egg-readonly marker files per shared/egg_container/__init__.py lines 152-183). The selector needs to read one of these and short-circuit LKG lookup. If it forgets, read-only phases will read a sidecar that may be stale-but-green from another sandbox — still correct (green is green) but violates the design intent (per Q13 rationale) of not reading cross-sandbox sidecars from a narrowing context.
affected_files: sandbox entrypoint (if it needs to surface role to selector)

mitigation.strategy: Selector checks for `.egg-readonly` marker in repo root OR EGG_AGENT_ROLE matching a known read-only role list (refiner, reviewer_*). If read-only, skip sidecar, use base branch. Log 'read-only role: using base branch baseline'. Add unit tests for both detection paths.

risks.title: Makefile test-all vs test split may diverge over time (docs rot)
risks.impact: docs/guides/testing.md (new per Q11) is the canonical doc. As Makefile, selector, and CI workflows evolve, the docs can drift. Drift is especially dangerous for agents whose runbook is the docs.
risks.description: Standard documentation-sync risk. Repo already has docs/ convention and make help pointer.

mitigation.strategy: Add a test that asserts the Makefile help output includes a 'See docs/guides/testing.md' line and that docs/guides/testing.md exists. This is a cheap drift trap. Link CONTRIBUTING.md to the guide (one line + link per Q11).

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The gateway/tests/conftest.py importlib-based loading is a documented peculiarity of this repo that creates a static-analysis blind spot. The plan must explicitly map gateway/*.py → gateway/tests/ rather than rely on decision-10's generic dynamic-import widening, which does not reach these edges. This is the single highest-likelihood correctness failure mode.
areas_requiring_human_review.suggested_reviewer: Reviewer familiar with gateway/tests/conftest.py's custom module loader (see gateway/tests/conftest.py::_load_module_with_replaced_imports)

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: AC-2 (shared/ changes pull tests across all consumers) depends on every repo root being passed to grimp.build_graph. The task plan must list them explicitly, and the selector must assert every .py file under those roots resolves to a graph node.
areas_requiring_human_review.suggested_reviewer: Reviewer with whole-repo awareness of source roots

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: Q5 recommended inferring 'explicit file path' from PYTEST_ARGS; an explicit EGG_TEST_SELECT=off env var is more robust. Confirm the plan's choice and its test coverage.
areas_requiring_human_review.suggested_reviewer: Reviewer with familiarity with developer UX conventions

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: Decision-2 flips CI to test-all, but other workflows, scripts, and docs may also invoke `make test` expecting full-suite behavior. Confirm a grep pass was done.

rollback_plan.strategy: Changeset-awareness is fully reversible by reverting the PR. Sidecar directory (.egg-state/last-known-good/) is gitignored, so no state is in history. grimp is a dev-only dep pinned in pyproject.toml; removing it on revert drops the import. No data migration, no schema change, no production-runtime change.
steps: 1. Revert the PR via GitHub UI (creates revert commit).
2. `make test` returns to running the full suite (pre-change behavior).
3. `make test-all` / `make test-record-good` targets disappear (were added in this PR).
4. grimp drops from uv.lock on next `uv sync`.
5. .egg-state/last-known-good/ sidecar files remain on disk but are ignored — safe to leave or `rm -rf`.
6. CI workflows (.github/workflows/test.yml) are already switched to `make test-all` per decision-2 — revert restores `make test` there too.
7. No manual intervention to running sandboxes; they pick up the new Makefile on next image rebuild.
rollback_plan.data_loss_risk: NONE — no persistent data is affected. Sidecar is ephemeral per design.
rollback_plan.downtime_risk: NONE — changes are developer/CI tooling only, no runtime service impact.
rollback_plan.partial_rollback_option: If only the canary behavior is problematic, ship a follow-up that sets the canary cadence to 1 (every run = full suite), effectively reverting narrowed behavior while keeping the infrastructure in place.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Hard-code the gateway/*.py → gateway/tests/ mapping (R1) as an explicit fallback-trigger rule in the selector, documented as a known static-analysis blind spot. Do not rely on decision-10's generic 'reachable from dynamic-import module' widening — the reachability relation is degenerate here.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Correctness-first. This is the single most concrete false-negative path; the mapping is small, stable, and testable.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Enumerate every repo root that grimp.build_graph receives (gateway, shared, orchestrator, sandbox, sandbox/tools, tests, tests/*/). Add a self-check: every .py file under those roots must appear in graph.modules; any missing file → log + fall back to full suite.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: AC-2 hinges on this. The self-check turns silent failures into loud fallbacks.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Filter the selector's OUTPUT to the existing `make test` universe (tests/ + gateway/tests/ + orchestrator/tests/ + shared/tests/, `not functional`). Do not let graph reach expand the scope beyond what `make test` already runs.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Preserves reproducibility; avoids accidentally adding sandbox/tests/ or scripts/tests/ to the default path.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Introduce `EGG_TEST_SELECT=off` env var opt-out instead of (or in addition to) PYTEST_ARGS inference for Q5. Document in docs/guides/testing.md.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Robust, explicit, unambiguous. Removes shell-parsing fragility.

performance_assessment.graph_build_cost: grimp 3.x Rust backend on ~771 files with cache: <500ms warm, 1-5s cold. Cache path under .egg-state/grimp-cache/ keeps it warm across sandbox recreations.
performance_assessment.selection_compute_cost: Reverse transitive closure is near-linear in graph size after grimp's Rust build step — negligible relative to pytest wall time.
performance_assessment.pytest_savings_ceiling: Uncertain without a hard target (per Q1 — intentional). Branches touching a leaf gateway module should see selection go from ~149k LOC of tests down to the test files in gateway/tests/ that transitively import that module (plus conftest widening). Rough expectation: 10-50x speedup for leaf changes; 0x speedup (full suite) for conftest/Makefile/docs/.python-version/shared-fixture changes.
performance_assessment.logging_overhead: One stderr line + one JSON file write per invocation — negligible.
performance_assessment.worst_case_latency: Full suite + grimp overhead (a few seconds slower than status-quo `make test`). Acceptable — fallback path only triggers on cases that were always going to be slow.
performance_assessment.measurability_plan: Per Q1, instrument and log selected_count, total_count, selection_compute_ms, pytest_wall_ms. Aggregate from .egg-state/selection/*.json across real runs; set a concrete target in a follow-up.

security_assessment.threat_model: Narrowing test selection does not change the application trust boundary. The selector reads git history, scans .py files with grimp, and writes to .egg-state/ (already gitignored, already writable by all roles). It does not execute untrusted code and does not introduce new network calls. grimp itself executes Python-level parsing over repo .py files; it does NOT import them, so it cannot be subverted by malicious `__init__.py` code.
security_assessment.gateway_policy_interaction: Decision-8's resolution was to make the LKG untracked (sidecar), which sidesteps the gateway role-boundary push policy entirely. The .egg-state/ prefix is already a permitted push target for producer roles (it's in the RISK_ANALYST and other role allow lists). The selector itself never pushes anything.
security_assessment.supply_chain: grimp 3.x: no known CVEs (Snyk 2025-10-02); 116k weekly downloads; maintained by David Seddon; uv.lock pins the version; dev-only, not shipped in production containers. Low risk.
security_assessment.residual_risk: NEGLIGIBLE — no new trust boundary crossed.

compatibility_assessment.breaking_changes: `make test` behavior flips from full-suite to changeset-aware. Mitigated by decision-7 (`make test-all` escape hatch), decision-2 (CI flip), and REC6 (audit + banner).
compatibility_assessment.backward_compatibility: Preserved via `make test-all`. Env-var opt-out (REC4) lets any caller force full-suite behavior locally without Makefile edits.
compatibility_assessment.forward_compatibility: Good — selector is a separate module with clear entry point; future optimizations (pytest-testmon, allowlisted non-.py paths, fine-grained shared-fixture mapping) land as follow-ups without touching the core interface.
affected_systems: Local developer workflow (`make test` changes default)
CI unit-tests job (`.github/workflows/test.yml` — flipped to test-all by decision-2)
Other CI workflows that invoke `make test` (audit per REC6)
Sandbox agents' inner-loop feedback (new narrow behavior; canary every 10th + full suite at CI)
